blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke sawal kis qisam ka hai: upar sirf 1 hai aur neeche \(x^2 - 1\), yani proper fraction (sahi kasr). Neeche wala hissa do mukhtalif linear factors mein toot jata hai, is liye yeh Case I hai.
Humein yeh fraction do aasan fractions ke jama (sum) ki shakal mein likhna hai.
Plan: pehle \(x^2 - 1\) ke factor banayenge, phir identity likhenge, factors ke zero rakh kar \(A\) aur \(B\) nikalenge, aur aakhir mein fractions wapas jor kar tasdeeq karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 1}\)
Maloom karna hai: is ke partial fractions (juzvi kasoor).
Tareeqa: Case I, yani non-repeated linear factors. Har linear factor ke neeche ek fraction banta hai jis ke upar ek unknown constant hota hai. Yeh constants hum identity se nikalte hain. Identity woh barabari hai jo \(x\) ki har value par sach hoti hai, is liye hum apni marzi ki aasan values rakh sakte hain.

Pehle check karein ke fraction proper hai ya nahi
Upar (numerator) ki degree 0, neeche (denominator) ki degree 2.
Kyun: Partial fractions seedha sirf proper fraction ke banaye jate hain, yani jab upar ki degree neeche se kam ho. Yahan \(0 < 2\) hai, is liye division ki zaroorat nahi. Yeh check har sawal mein sab se pehle karein, warna aage ka saara kaam ghalat ho sakta hai.

Denominator ke factors banayein
\[x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\]
Kyun: Yeh difference of squares (do squares ka farq) hai: \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\). Yahan \(a = x\) aur \(b = 1\) hai. Jab tak neeche ke factors saamne na hon, hum fractions ki shakal decide nahi kar sakte.

Partial fractions ki shakal likhein
\[\dfrac{1}{(x - 1)(x + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1}\]
Kyun: Do mukhtalif linear factors hain, to do fractions banenge. Har ek ke upar sirf ek constant aata hai, kyunke linear factor ke neeche wale fraction ka numerator us se ek degree kam, yani sirf number, hota hai.

Denominators hata kar identity banayein
Dono taraf \((x - 1)(x + 1)\) se multiply karein:
\[1 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 1) \quad (i)\]
Kyun: \(A\) ke neeche \((x - 1)\) cancel ho jata hai aur \((x + 1)\) bach jata hai; \(B\) ke neeche \((x + 1)\) cancel ho kar \((x - 1)\) bachta hai. Asaan yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: har constant ke saath woh factor lagta hai jo us ke apne fraction ke neeche nahi tha.

\(A\) nikalein: (i) mein \(x = 1\) rakhein
\[1 = A(1 + 1) + B(0)\]
\[1 = 2A\]
\[A = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) par \(x - 1 = 0\) ho jata hai, is liye \(B\) wala poora term zero ban kar ghayab ho jata hai aur sirf \(A\) bachta hai. Isi liye hum factor ka zero hi rakhte hain: ek hi qadam mein ek constant mil jata hai.

\(B\) nikalein: (i) mein \(x = -1\) rakhein
\[1 = A(0) + B(-1 - 1)\]
\[1 = -2B\]
\[B = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x = -1\) par \(x + 1 = 0\), to \(A\) wala term khatam ho jata hai.
Dhyan dein: \(-1 - 1 = -2\) hai; yahan sign ki ghalti bohat aam hai, is liye bracket ka hisaab alag likh kar karein.

Coefficients compare karein (doosri tasdeeq)
(i) ko khol kar likhein: \(1 = (A + B)x + (A - B)\).
\[x:\ A + B = 0\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[\text{const}:\ A - B = 1\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: (i) identity hai, is liye dono taraf \(x\) ki har power ke coefficients (sath lage numbers) barabar hone chahiyein. Yeh wohi theorem on equal polynomials hai jo kitaab ne 5.1.2 mein bataya. Baayen taraf \(x\) wala term hai hi nahi, is liye us ka coefficient 0 hai.

Jawab likhein
\[\dfrac{1}{x^2 - 1} = \dfrac{1}{2(x - 1)} - \dfrac{1}{2(x + 1)}\]
Kyun: Shakal mein \(A = \tfrac{1}{2}\) aur \(B = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) rakh diye. Upar \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) likhna aur neeche 2 likhna ek hi baat hai; minus wala constant jama ko tafreeq (subtraction) bana deta hai.

Tasdeeq: fractions wapas jor kar dekhein
\[\dfrac{1}{2(x - 1)} - \dfrac{1}{2(x + 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{(x + 1) - (x - 1)}{2(x - 1)(x + 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{2(x^2 - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 1} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Partial fractions asal mein ulta kaam hai: agar hum unhein common denominator par jor dein to asal fraction wapas milna chahiye. Agar na mile to kahin ghalti hai.
